subtitle: One meaning, another grammar, and a report in the nominal style
words.intro: Germany has a form for most things, and a form for the things without forms. To be at home here is to read one sentence in three different grammars, and to know they all mean: pay by Friday.

grammar[0].fact: Reformulating is a standard task in C1 exams and at any German office. Why does anyone need it? Because a good official sentence must hold up in court, and a plain one must be understood by the person it’s for. Rarely are those the same sentence.

grammar[1].subheading: Clause to phrase, and not overdoing it
grammar[1].blocks[0].note: No article? The describing word shows the case: fehlender, starker.
grammar[1].blocks[1].title: Don’t overdo it
grammar[1].blocks[1].text: Two or three noun chains per paragraph are enough. Four genitives in a row lose the reader.
grammar[1].blocks[2].title: Words for the practice page
grammar[1].fact: A report in the nominal style uses far fewer words than a story, which is why offices like it. But it’s easy to overdo: more than two nouns in a row, and you’ve lost your reader. The rule that editors give: if you can’t read it aloud, cut it.

document.intro: A real set of house rules, from a home for the poor in Hannover. It’s a lesson in sentence shapes: *ist … untersagt*, *sind zu vermeiden*, *dürfen … werden*. Find the sentence about what mustn’t go out of the window, and the one about the piano.
document.fact: Institutions have used this style of order for a very long time, and it has survived almost unchanged. Your own *Hausordnung* today probably mentions the same quiet hours and forbids the same things, though it’s less likely to bring up vermin.
document.tasks[1].items[2].prompt: Es darf nichts aus dem Fenster geworfen werden. (man)
reading.intro: Vroni’s friend Timo has got a job at the town hall. His first task: a notice saying that dog owners must register their dogs. His boss, Frau Amtmann Weigel, has marked it in green. Timo has now written three versions, and all three say the same thing.
reading.photos[1].caption: Ein Amtsgebäude: Der Antrag ist in dreifacher Ausfertigung einzureichen.
reading.fact: Most towns collect a *Hundesteuer*, a tax on dogs, which goes back a long way. There’s no tax on cats, though it’s sometimes proposed. Your dog gets a small metal tag to wear, and the tax can rise steeply for the second one.
